title: Authority Core — fast rule compiler + async audit bridge for API & Console
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Objective: Build 'Authority Core', a compact policy compilation and evaluation engine paired with an asynchronous audit bridge and runtime authorization middleware that can be embedded into the API gateway, runtime request path, and Console backend. The goal is to replace the heavyweight policy-service pattern with a low-latency, cache-friendly evaluator for RBAC v2 rulesets and produce consistent, tamper-evident audit events for admin actions and policy decisions.

Background: Existing authorization flow relies on a remote policy-orchestrator causing 10-30ms p99 amplification on hot paths and occasional timeouts during failovers. Audit events are emitted synchronously from multiple services in different formats which makes forensic analysis and retention policy enforcement difficult. We need a compact runtime representation of RBAC rules, deterministic evaluation order, and a single audit bridge that standardizes payloads and writes to our audit pipeline asynchronously (with retry/backpressure).

Scope & Success Criteria:
- Implement a policy compiler that turns declarative RBAC v2 rules (roles, grants, resource patterns, contextual predicates) into a runtime decision DAG that can be serialized and cached per deployment/cluster.
- Provide a middleware shim for API gateway, runtime inference path, and Console backend that evaluates compiled policies with <2ms median decision latency on representative p3-small instances and <10ms p99.
- Build an async audit bridge that accepts decision records and admin action events, enriches them with request context (actor, token metadata, model/version, route), and emits newline-delimited JSON to our audit sink with guaranteed once-or-more delivery semantics and observable retry/backoff.
- Provide feature flags and config hooks for canary rollout, sampling (rate-limited audit), and fallback to remote-orchestrator on cache miss or degraded local evaluator.
- Add tests: unit, decision-property fuzzing, integration with SSO flows (SAML/OIDC), and chaos tests for degraded audit sink.

Out-of-scope for initial iteration: full policy editor UI in Console (we will wire into existing Console controls in a follow-up), fine-grained consent flows, and cross-cluster distributed policy synchronization (handled by separate syncer ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Compiled policy artifact format documented and versioned; artifacts can be loaded from disk or fetched by ID from config store
Local evaluator middleware integrates into API gateway and Console backend with feature-flag toggle
Median decision latency <2ms, p99 <10ms on target hardware (benchmarks attached)
Audit bridge emits standardized NDJSON with schema v1 and shows up in audit pipeline within retention SLA
Fallback path to remote policy service validated under simulated cache miss and degraded local evaluator
implementation_steps: Design: finalize on runtime artifact schema and simple decision DAG encoding (Aisha, 2026-02-12)
Prototype: compile small subset of RBAC rules to DAG, run microbenchmarks (Jordan, 2026-02-20)
Middleware: implement language bindings (Go for gateway, Rust shim for runtime, Node/Python for Console) and standardize API surface
Audit bridge: build async worker, retry/backoff, sample controls, transform to NDJSON schema v1
Integration: wire SAML/OIDC assertions into policy context, validate admin flows
Testing: unit/fuzz, integration with audit pipeline, failure-injection tests
Rollout: staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on latency/error > threshold
comments: 2026-02-11 Jordan Lee: Initial spike shows DAG encoding reduces evaluation allocations by ~70% vs. remote JSON policy parsing. Need to measure cold-start deserialization overhead.
2026-02-18 Aisha Raman: Added audit schema v1 draft to Confluence; includes actor token fingerprinting and kv-metadata for post-hoc grouping.
2026-02-25 Security Review (notes): Ensure KMS-wrapped token fingerprints are used when storing PII in audit events; redact raw tokens at source. @security-team to provide scrubber patterns.
2026-03-03 Infra: Benchmarks show median 1.3ms, p99 9.1ms on test cluster; observed GC spikes in Node Console shim under synthetic load — need pooling or moving to Rust shim.
2026-03-10 PM (Sara Kim): Confirmed compliance scope for EU customers requires audit retention 7 years for admin actions. Added retention config to audit bridge backlog.
2026-03-12 Design (Lena Ortiz): Console exposes 'Admin Audit' view wireframe; will consume NDJSON from audit-bridge and filter by actor/resource/time.
2026-03-14 Jordan Lee: Opened PR to add fallback to remote-orchestrator and added metrics: local_evaluator_hit, local_evaluator_miss, audit_bridge_retry_count
reviewer_feedback: @security-team: Approve design pending scrubbing rules and KMS integration for any PII. Recommend threat model session before rollout.
@infra: Suggest shipping a Rust-based evaluator for Console to avoid Node GC interference; gateway remains Go.
@pm: Request an emergency rollback plan in case audit pipeline processing introduces backpressure into request paths. Should be async-only on first pass.
notes: Trade-offs considered: synchronous auditing ensures ordering but increases tail latency. We deliberately choose async with best-effort ordering per-request to protect p99 latency.
We will version compiled policy artifacts to allow graceful rollout across Dedicated and Private deployments; artifact v1 is intentionally conservative (no predicate JS).
Observability: emit decision explain traces at sample-rate 0.1% to tracing pipeline and correlate with audit records using trace_id
Migration path: start with Console admin actions and non-customer-facing API routes, then expand to inference runtime once stable.
